description: HesabYar Phase 5 wave 3 — payment channels + settlement engine (5پ), per ADR 0003 + phased design (hesabyar-reference/phased-design-checklist-2026-11-17.md §1.3 + §3). Six stories in three waves (A: US-520 + US-521 in parallel; B: US-522 + US-523 + US-524 in parallel; C: US-525). Builds on branch ralph/phase-5-2 (Phase 5-2 complete 6/6, parent-verified: wave-end suite 2177 passed / 8 skipped / 0 failed as amended; Alembic head 0019; OpenAPI 146 paths; scope catalog 38; vitest 245/245; build 37 pages). Hard rules: fee % is entered manually per channel/contract, NEVER hard-coded (rate change = new contract version, past settlements keep the old rate); NO browser automation of bank/gateway portals (ADR 0003 round-2 update 4); BNPL receivable is from the GATEWAY, not the customer; settlement auto-post only after mandatory tie-out with the bank deposit.

acceptanceCriteria: The 4 local-suite failures are fixed: tests/contract/test_store_pipeline.py::test_cancel_of_posted_invoice_creates_credit_note_in_tryton, test_partial_refund_creates_partial_credit_note_in_tryton, test_auto_post_opt_in_posts_the_invoice_in_tryton, and tests/interfaces/test_rest_integrations_sync.py::test_webhook_then_sync_dedups. Root cause: fixed invoice dates collide with restored test data (Tryton: invoice date must be after 11/17/2026 because the sequence was already used for invoice 0029). Fix with DYNAMIC dates, same class as commit 1eac7b2 (sales tests). Verified by targeted re-run of exactly these 4 tests (parent re-verifies locally).

The 5 responsive.spec.ts failures are fixed: (a) mobile navigation — 'فروش و خرید' is a collapsible group BUTTON, not a link; the test expands the group then clicks the sub-link; (b) 3x overflow — /packaging takes ~39s to load against remote Supabase (proven by screenshot), the 30s heading wait is too short; waits raised; (c) keyboard-only journal creation — the account combobox 'حساب ردیف ۱' stays disabled; diagnose the journal editor's enable logic and fix whichever side (test or product) is at fault.

The §3.8 Tryton spikes are CLOSED and the decision documented in docs/tryton-spikes-520.md: (1) payment wizards (Process/Succeed with clearing date) reachable via REST or JSON-RPC only? (2) can the adapter set party=gateway + maturity_date=tranche due on each line? (3) amount_to_pay behavior with a Draft payment? (4) Pay Invoice with Invoice Payment Method — does Party stay the customer or can the gateway Party be set? Decision: path 1 (wizard-driven) vs path 2 (direct move via port). This decision GATES US-522.
Verification runs TARGETED tests only (story's own + directly affected + ruff + pyright); the full suite runs once at wave-end.

acceptanceCriteria: Models (one Alembic migration, linear chain): gateway_payment (§3.2الف: payment_channel_id, gateway_transaction_id, store order/payment refs, Tryton invoice/journal refs, customer_party_id, gross/fee/vat/net in integer IRR, contract_version_id, fee_rate_snapshot, sales_period_jalali, gateway_confirmed_at, source, canonical_event_id, status scheduled/settling/settled/partially_cancelled/cancelled; UNIQUE on (payment_channel_id, gateway_transaction_id)), settlement_tranche (§3.2: tranche_index/count, sales_period_jalali from gateway_confirmed_at, expected_window_start/expected_date, gross/fee/vat/net per tranche, state machine, Tryton receivable-line ref with maturity_date=tranche due, variance + reason, match method/confidence), settlement_event, bank_deposit, settlement_match (many-to-many with allocated amounts), settlement_exception, settlement_fee_record (§3.6), settlement_file_import + settlement_file_row (§3.2ب, UNIQUE on (payment_channel_id, file_hash_sha256)).

Versioned gateway_contract extended (§3.1): fee_timing (proportional default / upfront_first_tranche), fee_accrual_policy (at_sale default / at_settlement), settlement_model (monthly_lump/lump_2month/tranches_2/tranches_4/daily/working_days; BNPL default tranches_4, sale month is the anchor) + tranche_legs jsonb [{month_offset, payout_day, percent}], payout_window_start/end_day, payout_calendar (jalali/gregorian), working_day_adjustment, day_lag, grace_days_after_due, match_tolerance_irr, tieout_tolerance_irr, auto_post_policy (draft_only default / auto_post_within_policy) + auto_post_max_amount_irr, source_note. Fee % MANUAL, never hard-coded; a rate change creates a NEW contract version with an effective date; existing schedules stay with the version they were built from (immutable); bulk re-derivation only by explicit user action + audit log entry.

Tranche derivation at payment time from the ACTIVE contract version: due-date algorithm (Jalali due month = sale month + month_offset; due = payout_day of due month; working-day adjustment to the next working day when enabled); day-based models (SalamPay 10 working days, Sadad ~1 working day) via month_offset=0 + day_lag counting working days from gateway_confirmed_at; formulas fee=round(G×c), fee_vat=round(fee×v), net=G−fee−fee_vat, all integer IRR via MoneyIRR; net split per tranche_legs with LAST TRANCHE = REMAINDER (same rule for fee and vat shares, not just net); half-up rounding per row; rounding policy identical to the tax module (US-402).

Tranche state machine (§3.3): expected → due → confirmed → received → settled, plus partially_confirmed/partially_received, overdue (past due + grace → alert + escalation 7/30/60 days), cancelled (pre-settlement refund/cancel cancels remaining tranches; already-paid tranches are deducted by the gateway from later settlements as a negative adjustment row), exception (variance/unknown reference, linked to settlement_exception), written_off (human approval only, within policy cap, audit-logged).

Period reassignment: if a gateway file shows a transaction in a different sales month, sales_period is corrected and OPEN tranches re-derive; confirmed/received tranches are untouched; an informational period_reassigned exception is logged.

REST endpoints for channels/contracts/payments/tranches (read + manage) with new scopes; W1 scheduler job (Procrastinate) emits the expected→due transition at the due date. Needs F1, F3 (channel/contract registry), F2 (account_payment_clearing), S1, US-402 (fee VAT rate + rounding), holiday list (F3).

acceptanceCriteria: §3.5 journals posted through AccountingEnginePort, following the US-520 spike decision (wizard-driven path 1 or direct-move path 2): sale recognition (Dr gateway receivable gross / Cr sales revenue); fee + fee VAT at sale under policy A (default: Dr fee expense + VAT / Cr gateway receivable, balance = net); clearing transfer on tranche confirmation (Dr clearing / Cr receivable, net of tranche); bank receipt (Dr bank / Cr clearing); policy B (at settlement) as the configured alternative (fee recognised per tranche as it confirms).

Fee-variance adjustment move: if the gateway file shows a real fee different from expected, the difference is posted as an adjustment move (Dr/Cr fee expense + corresponding VAT against gateway receivable) — NEVER silently absorbed; always recorded as an exception with a reason.

Post-settlement refund: Cr revenue (sales return) against Dr gateway receivable; the gateway deducts from the next settlement or requests a refund per the contract. Partial refund (payment.refunded): the refunded amount is deducted FIRST from the payment's OPEN UNREACHED tranches (last tranche backwards), then — if it exceeds the open balance — as a negative adjustment (refunds_deducted_irr) on the next tranche of the same gateway; confirmed/received tranches are untouched; every refund adjustment is logged with a reason + the refund event reference.

Adapter: payment groups per settlement batch; succeed with the gateway deposit date as clearing date (per spike decision); party=gateway per line; maturity_date=tranche due. fee_vat_claimable=false until an official gateway invoice/Moadian record is verified (US-402 dependency).

Acceptance e2e: the §3.5 SnappPay worked example green end-to-end — 100,000,000 IRR sale in Aban, 10% fee → 10,000,000 fee + 1,000,000 VAT → 89,000,000 net in 4 tranches of 22,250,000 due 5 Azar/Dey/Bahman/Esfand; receivable from SnappPay decreases month by month: 89M → 66.75M → 44.5M → 22.25M → 0.

acceptanceCriteria: Import flow (C1): gateway portal Excel upload (SnappPay + manual) → validation/dedupe → fee calculated from the contract → accounting-effect preview → review-queue item → approve → payment.settlement.received canonical events. Idempotency on (gateway, transaction_id); file-hash dedupe (re-importing the same file is a no-op); every import has an import_batch_id (whole batch reversible/reviewable). Net Sale rows and totals are dropped at parse and logged.

Matching (C2–C7): exact transaction_id match when the file has detail; batch match (due tranches of the same gateway+period whose net sums to the event net within tolerance, FIFO by due date); bank-deposit matching in confidence order — (1) exact tracking ref in the bank narrative → auto-match, high confidence (opportunistic: whether Iranian bank narratives carry the gateway tracking number is UNVERIFIED, never the sole support); (2) amount + date within match_window_days (±2 default, per-contract) → auto-match if unique; (3) amount-only → review queue with ranked suggestions; (4) no candidate → deposit_without_file exception. Reverse matching C7: a bank deposit arriving before the gateway file attaches to expected tranches (received without confirmed) and the later file confirms it.

MANDATORY tie-out (C6) before auto-post: Σ confirmed tranche nets − Σ documented period deductions = Σ matched bank deposits (within tieout_tolerance_irr). Undocumented deductions are NOT deductions — they create an amount_mismatch exception. If tie-out holds and policy allows → auto-post the bank move (clearing → bank) and close tranches (settled). If not → the whole batch stays in exception and NO automatic posting happens.

All 11 exception types (§3.7: late_tranche, missing_deposit, partial_tranche, amount_mismatch, fee_mismatch, deposit_without_file, file_without_deposit, unknown_reference, overpayment, period_reassigned, cancelled_after_settlement) reach the UNIFIED review queue as settlement_variance, each with severity, linked tranche/event/deposit, expected vs actual amounts, status and resolution. Overpayment parks as an unallocated receipt and is NEVER auto-allocated to future tranches. No exception is ever resolved silently.

SnappPay monthly settlement Excel is parsed from email (IMAP) — no ToS risk. NO browser automation is built (ADR 0003 round-2 update 4 + principle 7). UNVERIFIED: SnappPay Excel currency (Rial or Toman) — resolved with the first real customer file; the import accepts a per-import currency setting.

acceptanceCriteria: ZarinPal: GraphQL transaction API (list + refund) + T+1 lump schedule; settlement query in GraphQL is UNVERIFIED and is not relied on.
Torob Pay: OAuth REST payment API (Verify/Refund/Inquiry/Callback — verified via the payvand client + official WooCommerce plugin; no public docs); settlement stays file + bank matching.
Snapp Pay: REST v2.1 (eligible/token/verify/settle/revert/status/cancel/update) for STATUS RECONCILIATION ONLY; settlement comes from portal Excel + monthly email.
DigiPay: UPG (tickets/business, purchases/verify with 3-minute window, purchases/deliver mandatory for BNPL, refunds) for reconciliation; settlement output is UNVERIFIED — to be asked of support.

Sadad (Melli): store-side capture + daily lump + manual import; no inquiry/refund API per payvand; Excel output UNVERIFIED. SalamPay: store-side capture + manual import; TWO contract models (10-working-day lump at 5% fee OR seller credit-line monthly at zero fee — read from the contract, never assumed).

Registry separation: basalam_marketplace (SalamAPI marketplace channel) is distinct from salampay; torob_marketplace is RESERVED and stays DISABLED until the Torob order API is verified, never mixed with the torobpay payment channel.

Gateway-verified callbacks create gateway_payment rows (US-521 models); a BNPL payment creates a receivable from the GATEWAY, not the customer. No gateway is assumed to have a settlement API or a server webhook — settlement is file-based for all of them.
userStories.description: As HesabYar I want each gateway's payment API connected for status reconciliation, so verified payments flow into the settlement engine while settlement itself stays file-based.
